presets.name: Privacy: no telemetry, error reports or feedback uploads
presets.summary: Turns off Anthropic usage metrics, error reports, session surveys and the /feedback upload path, one variable each, while keeping auto-updates.
presets.riskReason: DISABLE_TELEMETRY also stops feature-flag fetching, so flag-gated features (Remote Control, Claude-drafted feedback, PowerShell tool by default on Windows with Git Bash, among others) become unavailable.

sources.quote: Metrics never include your code, prompts, or file paths. Set DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 to opt out.
Set DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING=1 to opt out.
To disable these surveys, set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY=1.
To opt out, set the DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND environment variable to 1.
Claude Code turns some features on through feature flags it fetches from Anthropic. Claude Code skips that fetch in these sessions:

presets.name: Privacy: block all non-essential traffic
presets.summary: One switch that stops auto-updates, telemetry, error reporting, /feedback, release notes and other non-essential network calls.
presets.riskReason: Also disables auto-updates and feature-flag fetching; you must run claude update yourself. Does not cover the WebFetch domain check or marketplace auto-install.

sources.quote: You can turn each off individually with the environment variables below, or disable all non-essential traffic at once by setting CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC.
Set to any non-empty value, such as 1, to disable nonessential network traffic: auto-updates, telemetry, error reporting, the /feedback command
This variable doesn't affect the WebFetch check or official plugin marketplace auto-install

presets.name: Privacy: keep local transcripts for 7 days
presets.summary: Deletes local session transcripts (stored in plaintext under ~/.claude/projects/) after 7 days instead of the default 30.

sources.quote: Claude Code clients store session transcripts locally in plaintext under ~/.claude/projects/ for 30 days by default to enable session resumption. Adjust the period with cleanupPeriodDays.
Delete session transcripts and other local session data after 7 days

presets.note: Sessions older than 7 days disappear from /resume.

presets.name: Protect secrets: deny reading .env and secrets/
presets.summary: Denies Claude reads of the project's .env files and secrets folder, as in Anthropic's example team settings.

sources.quote: Deny reads of env files and the secrets folder by the file tools and file-reading commands

Use it for files that hold API keys, secrets, or environment values: Claude Code excludes matching files from file discovery and search results, denies reads of them, and blocks the Edit and Write tools on the matching paths.
Read(./.env) on its own stops the file tools and commands that name the file, such as cat .env, but not grep -r run over the directory; the sandbox block in this file closes that gap

presets.note: Deny rules don't stop commands that read files without naming them (grep -r); pair with a sandbox preset for OS-level enforcement.

presets.name: Protect home-directory credentials (Trail of Bits list)
presets.summary: Denies reads of SSH/GPG keys, cloud, registry and git credentials, keychains and wallets, and edits to shell config and ~/.ssh.

sources.quote: Hardening reads: The settings.json template includes Read and Edit deny rules that block access to credentials and secrets:
Shell config -- ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc (edit denied, prevents backdoor planting)

Without /sandbox, deny rules only block Claude's built-in tools -- Bash commands bypass them. With /sandbox enabled, the same rules are enforced at the OS level (Seatbelt/bubblewrap), so Bash commands are also blocked. Use both.

presets.note: The Edit and Read deny entries of Trail of Bits' settings.json at commit 2109be9 (2026-08-24), without its Bash deny rules.

presets.name: Sandbox: hide AWS/SSH credentials and tokens from commands
presets.summary: Turns on the Bash sandbox and blocks sandboxed commands from reading ~/.aws/credentials and ~/.ssh or seeing GITHUB_TOKEN and NPM_TOKEN.
presets.riskReason: Sandboxed commands that need these credentials (aws CLI, git over SSH, npm publish) fail; the sandbox doesn't run on native Windows.

sources.quote: The example below blocks reads of the AWS credentials file and the SSH directory and removes GITHUB_TOKEN and NPM_TOKEN from the environment of sandboxed commands:
There is no built-in credential deny list, so only the files and variables you list are restricted.
The sandbox runs on macOS, Linux, and WSL2. On native Windows, Claude Code runs commands unsandboxed.

presets.name: Strip credentials from subprocess environments
presets.summary: Removes credential variables from the environment of Bash commands, hooks and stdio MCP servers that Claude Code starts.
presets.riskReason: Tools that read credentials from env vars stop working inside Claude, and it turns sandbox auto-allow off.

sources.quote: Set to 1 to strip credentials from the environments of the subprocesses Claude Code starts, such as Bash commands, hooks, and stdio MCP servers.
To strip credentials from all subprocesses regardless of sandboxing, set CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB.
CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB turns auto-allow off

presets.note: GitHub tokens and proxy settings are left in place by design.

presets.name: Disable bypass-permissions mode
presets.summary: Rejects --dangerously-skip-permissions and agent definitions that ask for bypassPermissions.

sources.quote: Prevent anyone from entering bypassPermissions mode. Claude Code then rejects the --dangerously-skip-permissions flag
"disableBypassPermissionsMode": "disable"

presets.name: Keep file tools inside the working directories
presets.summary: Claude's file tools refuse reads and writes outside the folders you work in, in every permission mode.
presets.riskReason: Needs Claude Code v2.1.314+ for the write block, removes the EnterWorktree/ExitWorktree tools, and other folders need /add-dir. Shell commands are not limited unless the sandbox is on.

sources.quote: Make Claude's file tools refuse reads outside your working directories in every permission mode, including bypassPermissions.
Make the Write, Edit, and NotebookEdit tools refuse paths outside your working directories in every permission mode, including bypassPermissions
Once the key is on, Claude Code also removes the EnterWorktree and ExitWorktree tools or refuses calls to them.

presets.name: Sandboxed Bash with fewer prompts
presets.summary: Runs Bash commands inside the OS sandbox and lets sandboxed commands run without a permission prompt.
presets.riskReason: Sandboxed commands, including ones that modify files inside the working directory, run without asking; on native Windows commands run unsandboxed.

presets.name: Strict sandbox (no unsandboxed fallback)
presets.summary: Turns the sandbox on, refuses to start if it can't run, and stops Claude from retrying blocked commands outside it.
presets.riskReason: Claude Code exits at startup on native Windows or where bubblewrap/socat are missing; tools incompatible with the sandbox can't run unless added to excludedCommands.

A false in your user settings, --settings, or managed settings holds even when a project's settings set true.
The sandbox doesn't run on native Windows, so with failIfUnavailable set, Claude Code exits at startup on those machines.

presets.name: Enterprise-like lockdown (Anthropic settings-strict example)
presets.summary: No bypass mode, every Bash command asks, web search/fetch denied, and the sandbox can't be weakened, from Anthropic's settings-strict.json.
presets.riskReason: Every Bash command needs approval and Claude loses web search and fetch.

presets.name: Desktop notification when Claude needs input (macOS)

sources.quote: Get a desktop notification whenever Claude finishes working and needs your input, so you can switch to other tasks without checking the terminal.

This command opens a dialog box rather than a notification in the corner of your screen, so the dialog can open behind your terminal window.

presets.name: Trail of Bits settings.json (as published)
presets.summary: Trail of Bits' opinionated defaults: targeted telemetry opt-outs, credential and destructive-command deny rules, rm -rf and push-to-main blocking hooks, one-year history.

hooks.command: CMD=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command'); if echo "$CMD" | grep -qiE '(^|;[[:space:]]*|&&[[:space:]]*|[|][|][[:space:]]*|[|][[:space:]]*)rm[[:space:]]' && echo "$CMD" | grep -qiE '(^|[[:space:]])-[a-zA-Z]*[rR]|--recursive' && echo "$CMD" | grep -qiE '(^|[[:space:]])-[a-zA-Z]*[fF]|--force'; then echo 'BLOCKED: Use trash instead of rm -rf' >&2; exit 2; fi
CMD=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command'); if echo "$CMD" | grep -qE 'git[[:space:]]+push.*(main|master)'; then echo 'BLOCKED: Use feature branches, not direct push to main' >&2; exit 2; fi

presets.riskReason: Turns on experimental agent teams (more token use), disables telemetry and so feature-flag fetching, and its hooks need jq and a POSIX shell. Trail of Bits pairs it with bypass mode plus sandboxing, which this preset doesn't set.

sources.quote: Opinionated defaults, documentation, and workflows for Claude Code at Trail of Bits.

env (privacy) -- disables three non-essential outbound streams: Statsig telemetry (DISABLE_TELEMETRY), Sentry error reporting (DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING), and feedback surveys (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY). Avoid the umbrella CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC -- it also disables auto-updates.

enableAllProjectMcpServers: false -- this is the default, set explicitly so it doesn't get flipped by accident. Project .mcp.json files live in git, so a compromised repo could ship malicious MCP servers.
cleanupPeriodDays: 365 -- keeps conversation history for a year instead of the default 30 days, so /insights has more data
hooks -- two PreToolUse hooks on Bash that block rm -rf and direct push to main
"CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH": "3"

presets.note: Exact settings.json at commit 2109be9 (2026-08-24) except $schema and statusLine, which points to a script (~/.claude/statusline.sh) you install separately from the same repo.
